digest.lead: Claude Code shipped two significant updates this week, introducing managed settings for enterprise teams and a bare scripting mode for automation workflows.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, a legal challenge to government restrictions on Anthropic continues, and the community is actively tracking Claude's growing impact on open source development.

stories.headline: Federal Judge Questions Government's Anthropic Ban as 'Punishment Attempt'
stories.summary: A federal judge criticized the U.S. government's restrictions on Anthropic, suggesting they appear to be punitive rather than regulatory in nature [1]. The legal challenge continues as the AI company faces government scrutiny.
stories.impact: This legal development could set important precedents for AI regulation and affect Anthropic's ability to operate and expand in government-adjacent markets.

sources.title: U.S. Government's Ban on Anthropic Looks Like Punishment Attempt, Judge Says

stories.headline: Claude Code Adds Enterprise Policy Management and Automation Features
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.83 introduced managed settings drop-in directories for team-based policy deployment and reactive environment hooks [1]. The previous v2.1.81 release added a --bare scripting mode that disables interactive features for automation workflows [2].
key_points: New managed-settings.d/ directory allows separate teams to deploy independent policy fragments that merge automatically
Added CwdChanged and FileChanged hook events for dynamic environment management
The --bare flag enables scripted operations without hooks, LSP, or plugin sync for CI/CD integration
stories.impact: These updates make Claude Code more enterprise-ready by enabling policy governance at scale and better automation integration for development teams.

stories.headline: New Site Tracks 19 Million Claude-Generated Commits on GitHub
stories.summary: A community project called Claude's Code has launched to track the massive scale of Claude's contribution to open source development, monitoring over 19 million commits generated by Claude on GitHub [1]. The project provides visibility into Claude's impact on the software development ecosystem.
stories.impact: This tracking effort highlights Claude's growing influence in open source development and provides valuable metrics for developers and organizations evaluating AI coding tools.

sources.title: Show HN: Claude's Code – tracking the 19M+ commits generated by Claude on GitHub

stories.headline: Developers Discuss AI Coding Tool Value Under Budget Constraints
stories.summary: A Hacker News discussion explores which AI coding models provide the best value for developers working with a $50 monthly budget [1]. The conversation reflects growing cost consciousness as AI coding tools become essential development infrastructure.
stories.impact: This discussion highlights the importance of pricing strategy for AI coding tools as they transition from experimental to essential development infrastructure for budget-conscious developers.

sources.title: Ask HN: $50 monthly budget, which coding models would you recommend now?

stories.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

stories.headline: Write a CLAUDE.md file to set project conventions once
stories.summary: Adding a CLAUDE.md to your project root lets you define coding standards, test commands, and architectural decisions that persist across every Claude Code session. Think of it as onboarding documentation that Claude reads automatically — you teach it once instead of repeating yourself.
actionable_steps: Create a CLAUDE.md in your project root with build/test/lint commands
Add coding conventions like naming patterns, preferred libraries, and file structure
Include architectural decisions and constraints Claude should respect
Use /init in Claude Code to auto-generate a starter CLAUDE.md

stories.headline: Use Claude's extended thinking for complex architectural decisions
stories.summary: When asking Claude to make non-trivial design choices — like choosing between patterns, structuring a new module, or planning a migration — enabling extended thinking produces significantly better results. Claude will reason through trade-offs before committing to an approach, catching issues that quick responses miss.
actionable_steps: For architecture questions, ask Claude to 'think through the trade-offs' explicitly
Use Claude Code's plan mode (shift+tab) for multi-step tasks that need careful reasoning
Review Claude's reasoning in extended thinking to catch flawed assumptions early

sources.title: Tips for getting better architectural advice from Claude
